name: Dumbbell Cross-Body Hammer Curl
grip: Neutral grip throughout, palms facing toward the torso, thumbs pointing along the dumbbell shaft.
description: Curl dumbbells diagonally across the torso toward the opposite clavicle while maintaining a strict neutral grip, placing peak mechanical emphasis on the brachialis and brachioradialis.
setup: Stand tall with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand beside your thighs with a neutral grip.
Keep your shoulders relaxed, chest proud, and core braced.
instructions: Curl one dumbbell diagonally upward and across your chest toward the opposite shoulder/clavicle.
Maintain a strict neutral hand position (thumb pointing upward and inward) throughout the entire path.
Keep your elbow stationary at your side without swinging it forward.
Squeeze your forearm and brachialis firmly at peak contraction near the opposite pectoral.
Lower the dumbbell under complete control along the same diagonal path back to your side before repeating with the opposite arm.
cues: Curl across the chest to the opposite collarbone.
Keep palm facing your torso throughout.
Pin elbow at your side, do not swing.
commonMistakes: Swinging the torso side-to-side to generate momentum.
Rotating the wrist into supination, turning the movement into a standard bicep curl.
Letting the elbow drift high into the air.

logging.example: Two 16 kg dumbbells used: record 16 kg per dumbbell.
logging.note: Record the mass of an individual dumbbell rather than the combined total pair mass.

variantNote: Cross-body variation of the hammer curl (also known as the pinwheel curl). Curling diagonally across the torso alters the line of pull to emphasize the brachialis and long head of the biceps.
